note: Charlemagne's imperial coronation (800) provoked Byzantine claim of sole Roman legitimacy; settled by Pax Nicephori (812).

_quarry.structural_significance: The rivalry over imperial title (800–812) forced each power to develop competing theories of universal sovereignty—papal-legitimated western empire versus continuous Roman succession—that defined the ideological framework of medieval political theory; the eventual recognition settlement created a permanent dual-empire conceptual framework that shaped canon law and political theology for centuries.
